lines: Jordan Lee
+1 (555) 010-2468 | jordan.lee@example.com | example.com/code/jordan-lee
EDUCATION
Western State University | M.S. in Computer Engineering | Metro City, USA | Sep 2024 - Expected Jun 2026
Eastern Institute of Technology | B.S. in Electrical Engineering | Metro City, Country | Sep 2018 - Jun 2022
EXPERIENCE
Eastern Robotics Co. | Junior Software Engineer | Metro City, Country | May 2023 - Jul 2024
- Rebuilt the diagnostics service's monitoring dashboards around per-sensor error budgets, cutting mean time to detect incidents from 40 to 12 minutes.
- Reduced p95 API latency from 420 ms to 180 ms by adding a request cache and batching sensor reads, with load tests that fail the build if p95 exceeds 200 ms.
- Maintained the CI pipeline for the perception team's model releases and adds automated regression checks that shortened release cycles to 3 days.

- Migrated 30 robot-fleet services from cron jobs to an event queue while rewriting the shared logging library, onboarding two new hires and taking over the weekend on-call rotation, which removed the nightly backlogs that delayed morning dispatch.
Mobility Systems Company | Machine Learning Engineering Intern | Metro City, USA | Oct 2024 - May 2025

- Built a diagnostics triage branch for an industrial inspection system that screens 800+ sensor signals per case with ML-extracted features, cutting the pending-case backlog 68% in the eight weeks after launch.
- Raised diagnostic accuracy on 1,200 held-out cases from 71% to 79% by fine-tuning a domain adapter on validated tool-use trajectories with assistant-only loss masking.
- Cut p95 latency of single-request edge inference by 40% by serving the INT8 engine with dynamic batching.
- Using grouped tool-use rollouts, a composite reward over accuracy, citation validity and call count, and a GRPO loop with a frozen SFT reference, reduced end-to-end latency 5%.
- Stabilised GRPO training on sparse rewards by sampling a single rollout per prompt, so each update used exactly one scored trajectory.
- Documented the triage branch's abstention rules and escalation paths for the on-call reviewers, who adopted them as the team's runbook.
PROJECTS
Agent Runtime Suite | Owner | TypeScript, Multi-Agent Systems | Aug 2025 - Present
- Drove adoption of AI-first engineering practices across the platform, accelerating delivery and improving outcomes for downstream teams.
- Cut p95 tool-call latency from 900 ms to 600 ms, a 50% reduction, by caching tool results and reusing completed sub-agent answers.
- Raised the runtime's task-completion rate by 12% on the benchmark suite, from 71% to 83%, by retrying failed sub-agent calls with their partial context.
Research-Agent Evaluation Framework | Contributor | LLM Evaluation | Feb 2025 - Jul 2025
- Upstreamed 8 citation and faithfulness metrics to an open-source research-agent framework, where they now run in the default benchmark for every release.
- Showed the evaluator tracks injected degradation with a Kendall correlation of 0.89 across 400+ report-level trials that removed citations, sources and claims.
- Traced 3 structural pipeline defects in stability, sourcing and parameter handling to their modules with layered instrumentation; each was fixed upstream.
SKILLS
Programming: Python, TypeScript, Git
ML & Agents: PyTorch, LoRA, GRPO, agent evaluation

items.says: Experience entries are not in reverse-chronological order.
items.because: The internship ending in May 2025 is newer than the role ending in July 2024.

items.says: Make the code link a complete, clickable URL leading directly to a relevant portfolio or profile.
Clarify “per-sensor error budgets” if it is internal terminology.
items.because: Readers may not understand what changed in the monitoring.

items.says: Keep the load-test threshold only if it demonstrates a lasting reliability improvement.
items.because: Otherwise, the measured latency gain should take priority.

items.says: “Maintained” and “adds” have inconsistent tenses.
items.because: The sentence reads as though the action is ongoing.

items.says: Give a baseline or clearer definition for the three-day release cycle.
items.because: Readers cannot judge how much it improved.

items.says: Break up or substantially shorten the crowded bullet.
items.because: It combines several kinds of work and an operational result, making ownership hard to follow.

items.says: Clarify what specifically eliminated the nightly backlogs.
items.because: The cause of the result is hard to follow.

items.says: Quantify the backlog or dispatch impact if possible.
Add the starting backlog scale or clarify how the 68% reduction was measured.
Clarify how the backlog reduction was attributed to the launch.
Explain “diagnostics triage branch” and “ML-extracted features” in plain terms.
items.because: Readers outside the team may not understand the system’s role.

items.says: Clarify how accuracy was defined.
Explain “assistant-only loss masking” for a general ML audience.
Make sure the held-out evaluation was independent of the tuning data.
Clarify the latency measurement setup, including whether individual requests were measured under concurrent traffic.
items.because: “Single-request” inference and “dynamic batching” can sound contradictory.

items.says: Reword the grammatically awkward opening construction.
Clarify what directly produced the latency reduction.
items.because: The sentence leaves the causal link unclear.

items.says: Specify the evaluation conditions for the latency result.
Explain how this latency result differs from the separate edge-inference result.
One rollout per prompt does not by itself mean each update used exactly one scored trajectory.
items.because: An update could contain multiple prompts.

items.says: Provide evidence of what “stabilised” means and what improvement was observed.
items.because: The bullet describes a method but not the observed improvement.

items.says: Use a consistent spelling convention for “stabilised.”
items.because: It uses British spelling.

items.says: Add evidence of runbook use or operational impact if available.
items.because: The outcome is less concrete than in the other bullets.

items.says: Replace “Multi-Agent Systems” with actual tools or frameworks used, if relevant.
items.because: It describes a field, not an implementation technology.

items.says: Specify your contribution to AI-first engineering practices.
items.because: The claim is broad compared with the rest of the résumé.

items.says: Substantiate adoption or impact, or remove the bullet.
items.because: “Improving outcomes” does not tell the reader what changed.

items.says: The reduction from 900 ms to 600 ms is 33.3%, not 50%.
items.because: The stated percentage does not agree with the absolute values.

items.says: The increase from 71% to 83% is 12 percentage points, not a 12% relative increase.
Give the benchmark’s scope or size if space allows.
items.because: Readers could better assess the result.

items.says: Consider mentioning the retry strategy’s effect on latency or cost.
Clarify your role in getting the metrics accepted if “upstreamed” does not convey it.
State what the Kendall correlation compares.
items.because: The statistic is hard to interpret without that context.

items.says: Identify the defects’ practical consequences or why fixing them mattered.
items.because: “Stability, sourcing and parameter handling” is vague.

items.says: Make clear what you personally traced or instrumented.
“Agent evaluation” is a capability rather than a specific tool or technology.
Consider including other role-relevant skills demonstrated by the experience.
items.because: The skills section is short.

items.says: Trim broad or lower-evidence claims if the résumé runs beyond one page.
items.because: It is an early-career résumé with several detailed technical bullets.

items.says: Standardize spelling, date formatting, punctuation, and capitalization throughout.
Check that final-document line breaks are natural rather than manually inserted mid-sentence.
